question: How many attention heads does the base Transformer use?
expected_answer: 8 heads

question: What BLEU score did the big Transformer achieve on WMT 2014 English-to-German translation?
expected_answer: 28.4 BLEU

question: How many layers does BERT-BASE have?
expected_answer: 12 layers (hidden size 768, 12 heads, 110M parameters)

question: Which two corpora were used to pre-train BERT?
expected_answer: BooksCorpus and English Wikipedia

question: Which retriever and which generator does RAG use?
expected_answer: DPR as retriever and BART as generator

question: What is the masked language model objective in BERT?
expected_answer: Some input tokens (15%) are masked at random and the model predicts the masked tokens

question: Why does the Transformer need positional encodings?
expected_answer: It has no recurrence or convolution, so positional information about token order must be injected

question: What is the difference between RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token?
expected_answer: RAG-Sequence uses the same retrieved document for the whole output sequence; RAG-Token can use a different document for each token

question: What is the next sentence prediction task in BERT?
expected_answer: A binary task predicting whether sentence B actually follows sentence A

question: Why does the Transformer scale the dot products by the square root of dk?
expected_answer: For large dk the dot products grow large and push softmax into regions with very small gradients

question: Describe the three different ways multi-head attention is used in the Transformer.
expected_answer: Encoder-decoder attention, encoder self-attention, and masked decoder self-attention

question: Describe the 80%, 10%, 10% masking strategy used in BERT pre-training.
expected_answer: A chosen token is replaced with [MASK] 80% of the time, a random token 10% of the time, and left unchanged 10% of the time

question: Explain how RAG combines parametric and non-parametric memory.
expected_answer: A pre-trained seq2seq generator is the parametric memory and a dense vector index of Wikipedia accessed by a retriever is the non-parametric memory

question: How is BERT fine-tuned for downstream tasks?
expected_answer: Task-specific inputs and outputs are plugged into BERT and all parameters are fine-tuned end-to-end

question: Describe the structure of the Transformer encoder and decoder stacks.
expected_answer: Each stack has N=6 identical layers; encoder layers have self-attention and a feed-forward sublayer, decoder layers add a third encoder-decoder attention sublayer
